# Centile plots

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from pcntoolkit import NormativeModel, NormData


# ============================================================
# PATHS
# ============================================================

current_dir = Path.cwd().parent

model_dir = (
    current_dir
    / "results"
    / "normative_model"
    / "BLR"
)

fig_dir = (
    current_dir
    / "results"
    / "figures"
)

fig_dir.mkdir(
    parents=True,
    exist_ok=True
)


# ============================================================
# LOAD MODEL + MODELLING DATA
# ============================================================

model = NormativeModel.load(
    str(model_dir)
)

model_df = pd.read_csv(
    current_dir
    / "results"
    / "combined_dataset"
    / "Model_dataframe.csv"
)


# ============================================================
# VARIABLES
# ============================================================

covariates = [
    str(x)
    for x in model.covariates
]

response_vars = [
    str(x)
    for x in model.response_vars
]

wanted = [
    "comp2",
    "comp10",
    "comp11"
]


# Batch effects used by the trained model
if model.has_batch_effect:
    batch_effects = list(
        model.batch_effect_counts.keys()
    )
else:
    batch_effects = []


# ============================================================
# CHOOSE ONE REAL REFERENCE PROFILE
#
# Important:
# We copy an ACTUAL animal/scan instead of setting all
# categorical dummy variables to 0.5.
# ============================================================

reference_df = model_df.copy()

# Use most common batch level
for be in batch_effects:

    reference_level = (
        model_df[be]
        .mode()
        .iloc[0]
    )

    reference_df = reference_df[
        reference_df[be] == reference_level
    ]


reference_df = reference_df.dropna(
    subset=covariates + batch_effects
)


# Choose animal closest to median age
median_age = (
    reference_df["Age(week)"]
    .median()
)

reference_index = (
    (
        reference_df["Age(week)"]
        - median_age
    )
    .abs()
    .idxmin()
)

reference_row = reference_df.loc[
    reference_index
]


# ============================================================
# FUNCTION TO CREATE VALID SYNTHETIC DATA
# ============================================================

def make_reference_dataframe(n):

    synthetic = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            col: [reference_row[col]] * n
            for col in covariates + batch_effects
        }
    )

    # Response values themselves are irrelevant when
    # computing model centiles
    for response in response_vars:
        synthetic[response] = 0.0

    return synthetic


# ============================================================
# AGE CENTILES
# ============================================================

age_min = model_df["Age(week)"].min()
age_max = model_df["Age(week)"].max()

age_values = np.linspace(
    age_min,
    age_max,
    150
)

age_df = make_reference_dataframe(
    len(age_values)
)

age_df["Age(week)"] = age_values


age_data = NormData.from_dataframe(
    name="Age_centiles",
    dataframe=age_df,
    covariates=covariates,
    batch_effects=batch_effects,
    response_vars=response_vars,
    remove_Nan=False
)


model.compute_centiles(
    age_data,
    centiles=[
        0.05,
        0.50,
        0.95
    ],
    recompute=True
)


# ============================================================
# SAVE AGE PLOTS
# ============================================================

x_age = (
    age_data.X
    .sel(covariates="Age(week)")
    .values
    .squeeze()
)


for component in wanted:

    lower = (
        age_data.centiles
        .sel(
            response_vars=component,
            centile=0.05
        )
        .values
        .squeeze()
    )

    median = (
        age_data.centiles
        .sel(
            response_vars=component,
            centile=0.50
        )
        .values
        .squeeze()
    )

    upper = (
        age_data.centiles
        .sel(
            response_vars=component,
            centile=0.95
        )
        .values
        .squeeze()
    )


    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=(5, 4)
    )

    ax.fill_between(
        x_age,
        lower,
        upper,
        alpha=0.15
    )

    ax.plot(
        x_age,
        lower,
        linestyle="--",
        linewidth=1
    )

    ax.plot(
        x_age,
        median,
        linewidth=1.5
    )

    ax.plot(
        x_age,
        upper,
        linestyle="--",
        linewidth=1
    )

    ax.set_xlabel("Age (weeks)")
    ax.set_ylabel("DR value")
    ax.set_title(component)

    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

    fig.tight_layout()

    fig.savefig(
        fig_dir / f"{component}_Age_centiles.svg",
        format="svg",
        bbox_inches="tight"
    )

    plt.close(fig)


# ============================================================
# SEX CENTILES
#
# Female  = Sex_M 0, Sex_Missing 0
# Male    = Sex_M 1, Sex_Missing 0
# Missing = Sex_M 0, Sex_Missing 1
# ============================================================

sex_df = make_reference_dataframe(3)

sex_df["Sex_M"] = [
    0,
    1,
    0
]

sex_df["Sex_Missing"] = [
    0,
    0,
    1
]


sex_data = NormData.from_dataframe(
    name="Sex_centiles",
    dataframe=sex_df,
    covariates=covariates,
    batch_effects=batch_effects,
    response_vars=response_vars,
    remove_Nan=False
)


model.compute_centiles(
    sex_data,
    centiles=[
        0.05,
        0.50,
        0.95
    ],
    recompute=True
)


# ============================================================
# SAVE SEX PLOTS
# ============================================================

sex_names = [
    "Female",
    "Male",
    "Missing"
]

x_sex = np.arange(3)


for component in wanted:

    lower = (
        sex_data.centiles
        .sel(
            response_vars=component,
            centile=0.05
        )
        .values
        .squeeze()
    )

    median = (
        sex_data.centiles
        .sel(
            response_vars=component,
            centile=0.50
        )
        .values
        .squeeze()
    )

    upper = (
        sex_data.centiles
        .sel(
            response_vars=component,
            centile=0.95
        )
        .values
        .squeeze()
    )


    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=(5, 4)
    )


    # 5th–95th centile range
    for i in range(3):

        ax.vlines(
            x_sex[i],
            lower[i],
            upper[i],
            linewidth=1.5
        )

        ax.hlines(
            lower[i],
            x_sex[i] - 0.08,
            x_sex[i] + 0.08,
            linewidth=1
        )

        ax.hlines(
            upper[i],
            x_sex[i] - 0.08,
            x_sex[i] + 0.08,
            linewidth=1
        )

        ax.scatter(
            x_sex[i],
            median[i],
            s=30,
            zorder=3
        )


    ax.set_xticks(
        x_sex
    )

    ax.set_xticklabels(
        sex_names
    )

    ax.set_xlabel("Sex")
    ax.set_ylabel("DR value")
    ax.set_title(component)

    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

    fig.tight_layout()

    fig.savefig(
        fig_dir / f"{component}_Sex_centiles.svg",
        format="svg",
        bbox_inches="tight"
    )

    plt.close(fig)


# ============================================================
# DONE
# ============================================================

print("Saved:")

for component in wanted:

    print(
        fig_dir / f"{component}_Age_centiles.svg"
    )

    print(
        fig_dir / f"{component}_Sex_centiles.svg"
    )
```
